_about: Boards and parts the lab works with and how each shows up on USB. tools/benchmark/detect.py and tools/arrival/arrival.py read it to name a board you plug in; 'usb' is the vendor and product id. Your own probe serials are not in this copy.

usb_families._about: How a vendor's board shows up on USB. VID:PID in hex, lower case. 'serial_hint' is a prefix seen on earlier TI boards of that family; a new TI board is confirmed by reading its chip id, never by the prefix alone.

ti-xds110.name: XDS110 Embed with CMSIS-DAP
ti-xds110.note: Every TI LaunchPad development kit with an onboard XDS110, and the LP-XDS110ET. Serial is 8 characters. Prefixes seen so far: MG35 (G3507), ML13 (L1306), LS45 (CC1354P10), CL37 (F2800137), LS47 (standalone probe). The LP-AM263P's probe is a TM4C1294-based XDS110 and should show the same 0451:bef3; add its prefix here after the first read. Identify the board with: /Applications/ti/ccs2101/ccs/ccs_base/common/uscif/xds110/xdsdfu -e, then a chip-id read with DSLite or OpenOCD. The IWRL6432BOOST's on-board XDS110 (TM4C1294) is expected here too (prefix not yet seen)

ti-xds110-bootloader.name: XDS110 in DFU mode
ti-xds110-bootloader.note: A probe mid firmware update. Do not touch; wait for it to come back as bef3

st-link.name: ST-LINK
st-link.note: 374b or 3752 is ST-LINK/V2-1 (TN1235 Rev 7 section 5.1), on the NUCLEO-G071RB (MB1360). The STLINK-V2EC on the NUCLEO-U083RC (MB1932) showed 0483:3752, firmware V2J43M28, and no mass-storage volume (read 2026-10-08). The rest are the V3 family. Both ST boards share this family: the plans tell them apart by chip id and the mass-storage volume name. Record the PID each board shows on arrival

nxp-mcu-link.name: MCU-LINK
nxp-mcu-link.note: FRDM-MCXA153's onboard MCU-Link, CMSIS-DAP mode. Verify on arrival

raspberrypi-rp2350-boot.name: RP2350 Boot
raspberrypi-rp2350-boot.note: Pico 2 held in BOOTSEL: a USB disk named RP2350 appears. Running a pico-sdk program with USB serial it shows as 2e8a:0009; running MicroPython as 2e8a:0005 (picotool 2.3.1 and MicroPython v1.29.0 sources, read 2026-10-07). No debug probe on the board

espressif-usb-jtag.name: USB JTAG/serial debug unit
espressif-usb-jtag.note: The ESP32-C6's own USB port. The DevKitC-1's second port is a USB-to-UART bridge (10c4:ea60 CP2102N on most revisions; verify on arrival)

cp210x.name: CP210x UART bridge
cp210x.note: USB-to-UART chip used on the ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1 UART port and many hobby boards

raspberrypi-rp2350-app.name: Pico 2 running a program (SDK USB serial or MicroPython)
raspberrypi-rp2350-app.note: A Pico 2 running a program with no USB code shows nothing at all

cp2108.name: CP2108 quad UART bridge
cp2108.note: SK-TDA4VM serial console J4 (four UART ports; the Linux console is the third). Seen 2026-10-09 on macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0): enumerates on USB but macOS creates no /dev/cu.* or /dev/tty.* ports for it, because no CP210x VCP driver is installed. Serial D0B8727BC62A038711EC24EEABE1C09. Other CP210x boards use other PIDs; auto_launch is off for this family.

ftdi-ft4232h.name: FT4232H quad UART bridge
ftdi-ft4232h.note: The TMDS62LEVM's UART port J7 (user guide SPRUJG8B table 2-24): A = SoC UART0 (console), B = SoC UART1, C = WKUP UART0, D = SoC UART4, 115200. macOS's built-in FTDI driver makes /dev/cu.usbserial-<serial>A to D. Serial not read; the EVM's XDS110 on J8 is the ti-xds110 entry
